newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary K&H bank boosts '96 profits, plans dividend.
newsitem.headline: Hungary K&H bank boosts '96 profits, plans dividend.

text.p: Hungary's K&H bank, slated for privatisation, boosted its profit and assets last year and plans to pay a dividend on its 1996 results, chief executive Janos Eros told a news conference on Friday.

Eros said 1996 was the first year K&H had been able to fill all its compulsory reserves and this will enable the bank to pay a 12 percent dividend on its 1996 results -- worth a total 40 million forints -- to holders of its priority shares.
"It is the first time ever for the bank that all its reserves have been filled," he said, adding that after filling the reserves there remained extra profit.
The dividend payment would remove the main barrier to the bank's improving its international credit ratings, he added.
The bank increased its balance sheet total to 360 billion forints in 1996 from 326.8 billion in 1995, while average inflation was 23.6 percent last year, the bank said in a statement.
After-tax profits grew to 2.7 billion forints last year from 1.9 billion forints in 1995, it said.
Eros said the bank pushed down the rate of qualified assets to 4.7 percent of all assets last year from 6.4 percent in 1995, to below the internationally accepted five percent level.
He added that the bank would continue its cost cutting programme and planned to keep the nominal value of all costs unchanged this year.
The government targets average inflation of some 17 percent for 1997.
K&H has reduced the number of its branches to 150 from 180 in January 1996, and plans to further cut this figure to 125, Eros said.
K&H plans to increase its pre-tax profit to four billion forints this year from 3.2 billion in 1996, and boost its balance sheet total to 384 billion forints by December 31, he said.

K&H also said that the European Bank of Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) would raise the capital of Hungary's Kereskedelmi Bank (K&H) by $30 million if a future strategic investor in Kereskedelmi agrees.
Hungary plans to privatise a stake of at least 25 percent plus one vote in K&H to a strategic investor this year.
